newsitem.title: USA: Lucent says Ameritech buys software units.
newsitem.headline: Lucent says Ameritech buys software units.

text.p: Lucent Technologies on Wednesday said Ameritech has purchased more than 500 of Lucent's Access Interface Units, or AIUs, which will help ease the battle for network access between Internet users and users making ordinary telephone calls.
A Lucent spokeswoman said the Ameritech contract marks the first commercial use of its Internet congestion relief system.

Northern Telecom Ltd offers a rival product, which SBC Communications Inc has said it plans to install on its five-state local network. Other local service providers have said they are considering such products.

Lucent's AIU is software, located in neighborhood-based central-office switches, that splits Internet traffic off of telephone lines for transmission over dedicated lines better suited to handling data-intensive communications.
By separating voice and data traffic, a phone company cuts down network congestion caused by the increasing volume of calls placed by computer users via modem to the Internet.

Industry experts say the Lucent and Northern Telecom equipment can help overcome the strain placed on existing phone networks, which were designed primarily to handle voice calls averaging around three to four minutes per call.
By contrast, they estimate that the typical Internet user remains on a line an average of 25 to 30 minutes per call.
Lucent said its Access Interface Unit is designed to offer high-capacity connections for calls with such long hold times.
The software has been tested at an Ameritech central office in Naperville, Ill., and will be used in other offices soon, officials of both companies said Wednesday.
Ameritech is in the process of installing the AIUs in switches in Illinois and Wisconsin, they said.
The AIU is essentially a software enhancement of Lucent's mainline central office telephone switch, the 5ESS Switch Module-2000.
The technology is considered a key element in reducing the possibility of blocked calls, an increasingly common complaint among phone customers.

"With the AIU, it's now possible to give consumers who make a lot of long calls -- such as those on the Internet -- their own dedicated circuit in a more cost-effective manner," said Dave Geary, regional vice president of Lucent Technologies.
